newsitem.title: FINLAND: FINLAND BANK HAS NO PLAN TO REVALUE GOLD.
newsitem.headline: FINLAND BANK HAS NO PLAN TO REVALUE GOLD.

text.p: Finland's central bank said on Friday it had no intention of revaluing its gold reserves in the wake of Germany's plans to do so.
"The Bank of Finland has no such plans," a spokesman told Reuters in response to a question. "Finland does not have such needs," he said.
The central bank, monitored by parliamentary supervisors but which takes independent monetary policy decisions, owns Finland's gold reserves, he said.
Finland's gold reserves weigh some 49 tonnes and their book value on April 30 was 1.7 billion markka, he said.
He declined to specify how the central bank values its gold but said it uses a certain markka value per gramme aimed at keeping the book value fairly close to the market value.
